claims.text: Local lattice distortion is a primary driver of mechanical-property differences among equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets.
Local chemical heterogeneity is a primary driver of mechanical-property differences among these alloys.
Changing constituent count changes local lattice distortion and chemical heterogeneity.
Local lattice distortion and chemical heterogeneity modulate dislocation mobility.
Local lattice distortion and chemical heterogeneity modulate grain-boundary strengthening or stability.
A greater constituent count produces greater local lattice distortion and chemical fluctuations.
Greater lattice distortion and chemical fluctuations impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion increases yield strength.
Greater lattice distortion may lower ductility by limiting dislocation recovery.
Greater lattice distortion and chemical fluctuations may promote stress concentration.
Alloys with fewer constituents have reduced lattice distortion.
Reduced lattice distortion facilitates easier dislocation glide.
Relative to equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni, quaternary and ternary subsets will have lower yield strengths.
Quaternary and ternary subsets may have higher ductility than the quinary baseline.
Quaternary and ternary subsets will exhibit altered failure modes relative to the quinary baseline.
Identical thermomechanical processing can produce comparable single-phase FCC grain structures across the quinary, quaternary, and ternary alloys under investigation.
Residual stresses and precipitate formation could also contribute to mechanical-property differences.
The proposed constituent-count mechanism should apply only while the alloys remain single-phase FCC and grain-boundary or impurity effects do not dominate deformation.

contradictions.description: The query states that the simple relationship between increasing constituent count and greater strength is no longer generally accepted, whereas the hypothesis predicts essentially that monotonic relationship: more constituents produce greater distortion and higher strength, while fewer constituents produce lower strength.

The query states that only nine of the 16 candidate alloys are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing, while the initial-state and conditions fields broadly describe all quinary, quaternary, and ternary samples as being processed into stable single-phase FCC structures. This could be resolved by explicitly limiting the study to the nine FCC candidates.
